##     message: "Iteration 84: ⚡ NATIVE BUILD CONFIG FIX — user reported app crashes INSTANTLY on freshly built EAS APK (CallDebugOverlay never appears at all). Engaged troubleshoot_agent for read-only RCA after multiple JS-level fixes had no effect. Root cause: Android release builds enable R8/ProGuard minification by default, which STRIPS `react-native-webrtc`'s native classes (`org.webrtc.**`, `com.oney.WebRTCModule.**`) because no keep rules were declared. The moment the JS code calls `require('react-native-webrtc')` or `new RTCPeerConnection()`, the stripped native classes cannot be loaded → instant native crash before any React UI mounts. This explains why JS-only fixes (iterations 82/83) could not resolve the crash. Compounding factor: `newArchEnabled: true` was set in app.json — react-native-webrtc@124.0.7 has known compatibility issues with React Native's New Architecture as of June 2025. ##     message: "Iteration 87: HEARTBEAT PING for unambiguous APK-presence verification. User correctly pointed out my timeline analysis was wrong — v2.1.10 was built 12:25 PM AFTER deployment at 12:15 PM, so the crash logger code WAS in v2.1.10. Yet no events arrived from Android. Most likely race condition: `recordDiagnostic` queues to AsyncStorage asynchronously via a Promise chain; the useEffect calling `flushDiagnostics()` runs on mount which may execute BEFORE the queued writes complete → events array is empty → return 0 → never sends. Fix: (A) Added new `sendDiagnosticHeartbeat()` function in /app/frontend/src/lib/diagnostics.ts that builds an in-memory payload `{events: [{tag:'HB', message: 'heartbeat from <platform>/<ver> app=<ver> device=<name>', source:'heartbeat'}, ...stored]}` and POSTs immediately — does NOT depend on AsyncStorage having any data. Also drains stored events piggybacked on the heartbeat. (B) Added eager call to `void sendDiagnosticHeartbeat()` at module-evaluation time (top of /app/frontend/app/_layout.tsx, alongside installGlobalDiagnostics) — runs the moment the JS bundle starts executing, before any React rendering. So if the diagnostics module is alive in the APK, the backend will see an `[DIAG][HB][heartbeat]` entry on EVERY app open, even if zero AsyncStorage writes succeed. Verified end-to-end: refreshed Metro web preview triggered backend log entry `[DIAG] session=00cbfd20... plat=web events=1` → `[DIAG][HB][heartbeat] heartbeat from web/0.0.0 app=2.0.0 device=?`. New build needed (v2.1.11) — user must Deploy + Generate new build. If after install + first launch we DO see an HB entry from plat=android in the supervisor log, diagnostics module is confirmed alive → any subsequent call-screen crash will leave a recoverable trail. If we DON'T see an HB entry at all, then the network call itself is being blocked (no internet permission, certificate pinning, wrong URL bundle, etc.) and we'd need a different approach (Sentry, Crashlytics, or in-app modal with copy-paste log box)."

##   - agent: "main"
##     message: "Iteration 93: 🎯 ROOT CAUSE FOUND & FIXED for the WebRTC native crash ('Smilers has stopped'). User shared 3 Sentry dashboard screenshots showing REACT-NATIVE-1 issue: 'TypeError: Super expression must either be null or a function' — fatal, unhandled, 10 events / 1 user, top stack frame `_inherits` (Babel's class-inheritance helper). The error is thrown by `_inherits(subClass, superClass)` when `typeof superClass !== 'function' && superClass !== null`, i.e., when something does `class X extends Y` where `Y` is `undefined`. Audited the codebase for class-inheritance candidates and traced the bug to a package.json override regression. (A) ROOT CAUSE: package.json had `overrides: { 'react-native-webrtc': { 'event-target-shim': '5.0.1' } }` and `resolutions: { 'react-native-webrtc/event-target-shim': '5.0.1' }` — forcing event-target-shim to v5.0.1. But react-native-webrtc@124.0.7 imports `{ Event }` as a named import from 'event-target-shim' in 6+ files (RTCTrackEvent.ts, RTCErrorEvent.ts, MessageEvent.ts, MediaStreamTrackEvent.ts, RTCDataChannelEvent.ts, RTCIceCandidateEvent.ts). Confirmed via `grep -E '^export|^exports\\.|^module\\.exports' /app/frontend/node_modules/event-target-shim/dist/event-target-shim.js`: v5.0.1 only exports `EventTarget`, `defineEventAttribute`, and `default` — NO `Event` class. So `import { Event } from 'event-target-shim'` resolved to `undefined`, and `class RTCTrackEvent extends Event` immediately threw 'Super expression must either be null or a function' at module-load time, killing the JS thread → 'Smilers has stopped'. The override was likely added in an earlier iteration to work around a different bundling issue but became counterproductive once react-native-webrtc gained additional named imports. (B) FIX: Removed both the `overrides` and `resolutions` blocks from /app/frontend/package.json. Ran `yarn install` — yarn now installs `event-target-shim@6.0.2` (react-native-webrtc's actual declared dependency). Verified the patch-rn-webrtc.js postinstall script ran successfully (44 files patched in react-native-webrtc, scanned 157) — it rewrites `event-target-shim/index` → `event-target-shim` to work around v6's strict exports field. Verified v6.0.2 exports ALL of: `Event`, `EventTarget`, `defineCustomEventTarget`, `defineEventAttribute`, `getEventAttributeValue`, `setErrorHandler`, `setEventAttributeValue`, `setWarningHandler`, and `default`. The `Event` class is now defined, so `extends Event` resolves to a real constructor function. (C) Restarted Expo, bundle compiles cleanly (Web 2331 modules, λ 2229 modules, HTTP 200), no Metro errors. ##     message: "Iteration 112: 🖥 SCREEN SHARING FINAL FIX — race condition in the screen-only bootstrap useEffect that survived iter-111's general WebRTC fix. After iter-111 changed the internal bail check in `startPeerConnection` from `initStartedRef.current` to `sessionRef.current` (correctly fixing regular call audio/video), screen-only mode STILL didn't work because the bootstrap useEffect at /app/frontend/app/call/[conversationId].tsx (lines 947-975) called `setCallId(conversationId)` and `void startPeerConnectionRef.current(asCaller)` synchronously in the same effect body. React state updates are async, so the closure of `startPeerConnectionRef.current` was created on the previous render where `callId === null`. The synchronous invocation hit the internal bail check `if (!callId || sessionRef.current || !CallSessionCtor) return` and bailed silently. Meanwhile `initStartedRef.current` had already been claimed (set to true) and the useEffect's deps didn't include `callId`, so the effect never re-fired after the state update propagated → PC was NEVER created → no offer, no media, screen sharing stuck on 'Connecting to screen…' forever. FIX: split the bootstrap into TWO useEffects. EFFECT A: when `isScreenOnly && conversationId && callId !== conversationId`, call `setCallId(conversationId)`. EFFECT B: when `isScreenOnly && callId === conversationId && peerUserIdParam && !sessionRef.current && !initStartedRef.current`, claim the slot via `initStartedRef.current = true` and invoke `startPeerConnectionRef.current(asCaller)`. By the time Effect B fires, the ref-sync useEffect has already refreshed `startPeerConnectionRef.current` with a closure that captures the up-to-date `callId`, so the function body proceeds past the bail check. Also added a fallback that releases `initStartedRef.current = false` on bootstrap error so future state changes can retry. Both sender (sharer) and receiver (viewer) paths benefit from this single fix. NO other code paths touched. Bundle compiles cleanly (Web 2341 modules); screen-share UI verified via web screenshots — sender shows pulsing broadcast circle + 'You're sharing your screen' + 'Stop sharing' + 'End screen share', receiver shows 'Watching shared screen' tag + 'Connecting to screen…' placeholder + 'Request to share my screen' + 'Leave screen share'. ⚠ Needs new EAS Android build to take effect on the user's device — no OTA. PLEASE TEST after rebuild: (1) /screen-share → pick contact → tap Send Share Request → recipient should get IncomingScreenShareModal → tap Accept → recipient's overlay should now show the live screen feed (NOT stuck on 'Connecting to screen…'). (2) Sender's diagnostic overlay should show: `[CALL] screen-only setCallId(xxxxxxxx…)` → `[CALL] screen-only mount role=sharer …` → `[PC] created (callType=video, isCaller=true, hasLocalStream=true, localTracks=2)` → `[SIG] → offer (sdp …B, recvVideo=true)` → ICE candidates → `[PC] state=connected`. (3) Receiver's diagnostic overlay should show: `[CALL] screen-only setCallId(…)` → `[CALL] screen-only mount role=viewer …` → `[SCRN] viewer-only: skipping initLocalMedia` → `[PC] created` → `[SIG] ← offer (processing …B)` → `[SIG] → answer` → `[PC] ontrack kind=video readyState=live` → `[PC] state=connected`. (4) Regular voice/video calls should ALSO continue working (iter-111 fix retained)."

Bundle compiles cleanly."

##     message: "Iteration 114: 📬 PUSH NOTIFICATIONS — eas.json misconfiguration fix + FCM credentials audit. User confirmed via Expo dashboard screenshot that the Firebase Admin SDK service account IS properly uploaded as Expo's FCM V1 push credential (Project ID smilers-a4e07, Client firebase-adminsdk-fbsvc@smilers-a4e07.iam.gserviceaccount.com). So the Expo→FCM→device delivery path is correctly wired at the platform level. HOWEVER discovered that the previous iter-108 'fix' had wired the SAME Firebase Admin SDK key into eas.json at `submit.production.android.serviceAccountKeyPath` — that field is for Google Play Console uploads ONLY (it expects a Play Console service account, NOT a Firebase Admin SDK one). The misplaced wiring would have caused `eas submit --platform android --profile production` to fail with a 401 against the Google Play API (Firebase key has no Play Console authority). FIX: removed the entire `submit` section from `/app/frontend/eas.json` (cleaner than leaving it half-broken). Rewrote `/app/frontend/eas.notes.md` end-to-end with the correct FCM v1 upload procedure (CLI `eas credentials --platform android` AND dashboard URL), explicit warning about the misplaced-key pitfall, separate guidance on how to wire Play Store submission credentials later (when the user creates a real Play Console service account), and rotation procedure. Bundle still compiles cleanly (Web 2342 modules, no schema validation errors on `eas.json`). NEXT STEP IS A FRESH BUILD: Their previous test build was made BEFORE the FCM V1 credentials were live at Expo, so device tokens acquired then might not route correctly. On the new build, instruct user to: (1) open app → grant notification permission, (2) navigate to Settings → Notifications, (3) verify under 'Push diagnostics' card that `Status: registered` AND `Push token: ExponentPushToken[...]` is populated, (4) tap 'Test local notification' → should fire a banner immediately (verifies device-side display), (5) tap 'Test remote self-push' → calls https://exp.host/--/api/v2/push/send with their own token → if 'Expo receipt is OK' appears AND the banner arrives, FCM V1 delivery is working end-to-end (any remaining 'not arriving' issue would be on the Smilers Convex backend side — it has to call Expo's push API when messages arrive, that's THE last unknown). If the 'Test remote self-push' DOES work, the bug is on backend, not client. If it does NOT work, the diagnostic value (Expo receipt error details) will tell us exactly what FCM is rejecting (token format, project mismatch, etc.) for iter-115 follow-up."

##   - agent: "main" Without the user's exact `[ERR] chat/scheduleMessageMobile × ...` log from their previous device, the agent took THREE measures to (a) unblock the user even if there's a backend rename, (b) bullet-proof arg coercion, and (c) capture exact rejection details on next failure. CHANGES TO /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx: (1) added `createScheduledLegacy = useMutation((api as any).scheduledMessages?.create)` as alternative endpoint reference; (2) aggressive arg coercion right before send — `safeRecipient` (typeof guard + trim + 200-char cap, falls back to 'Chat'), `safeMessage` (String() coerce + 5000-char cap), `safeDate`/`safeTime` (String() coerce); (3) wrapped the primary `createScheduledMessage(args)` call in its own try block that, on failure, captures `error.name`, `error.code`, `error.data` (where Convex puts ArgumentValidationError details) and logs them via recordDiagnostic with tag NET (`↻ primary failed name=X code=Y data=Z — trying scheduledMessages.create fallback`), THEN probes the legacy `scheduledMessages.create` endpoint; if that also fails, both failures are logged and the primary error is re-thrown for the catch block; (4) catch block now captures FULL diagnostic envelope — `name`, `code`, `msg`, AND `data` (stringified, 400-char cap). CHANGES TO /app/frontend/app/scheduled.tsx: (1) added `createScheduleLegacy = useMutation((api as any).scheduledMessages?.create)`; (2) `syncLocalDrafts` and `onSave` both wrap the primary call in a try/catch that falls back to `createScheduleLegacy(args)` on failure; (3) defensive arg coercion applied to both paths. Bundle compiles cleanly; /scheduled screen renders correctly via web preview. ⚠ Needs new EAS Android build to take effect. AFTER REBUILD, please retry scheduling from chat composer. If it STILL fails, open Settings → Diagnostic Logs and share the entry beginning `[ERR] chat/scheduleMessageMobile × name=... code=... data=...` — that `data=...` field will tell us exactly which validator on the backend is rejecting our payload so we can patch it precisely in iter-114."

##   - agent: "main" User reported that some replies preserve the parent-message context (the bubble shows the small inline quote pill on top) while others don't — comparing two replies sent moments apart, 'Thanks' showed the parent quote, 'Great' didn't. Root cause: the Smilers Convex backend uses `replyToId` per the public API spec the user shared in iter-100 (schema: messages → ...replyToId...; send mutation arg: ...replyToId?...), but our mobile client has historically been sending {replyToMessageId: ...} and reading item.replyToMessageId. Different deployments handle unknown fields differently — some Convex deployments accept and store extra fields (legacy / allowExtra mode) while strict ones drop them silently, which would explain why one reply preserved the parent and the next didn't (the answer flips when the deployment is upgraded or a different code path is taken). Belt-and-braces fix: SEND both names AND READ both names so the client works regardless of which schema the backend has settled on. (A) SEND-SITE NORMALISATION (8 mutation call-sites updated in /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx — text send, image send, voice note send, GIF send, scheduled message send, plus the edit-mode resend, location share, poll share): every `...(replyToMessageId ? { replyToMessageId } : {})` spread became `...(replyToMessageId ? { replyToMessageId, replyToId: replyToMessageId } : {})`. Also the analogous single-line {replyToMessageId: replyTo._id} variant on the broadcast path. Cost: one extra key on the payload, both unknown-field-tolerant on permissive backends AND first-class on the spec'd schema. (B) READ-SITE NORMALISATION (2 sites): the FlashList renderItem's parentMsg prop on MediaBubble at line 1789 now resolves `const parentId = item.replyToId || item.replyToMessageId; return parentId ? msgById.get(parentId) : undefined;` — robust to both historical mobile-written rows (replyToMessageId) and freshly-written or web-app-written rows (replyToId). Same change applied to the alt-bubble renderer's 'Replying to earlier message' fallback at line 2566: `msg.replyToId || msg.replyToMessageId`. (C) Bundle compiles cleanly: Web 2334 modules, λ 2234 modules. No behaviour changes to the reply UX itself — just guarantee the parent pointer is round-tripped on every payload regardless of backend schema variant. (D) Files touched: /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx (10 sites in total — 8 send-mutation spreads, 1 lookup, 1 fallback). NO changes to MediaBubble itself — its existing parentMsg-driven render is correct, it only got reliable data now. (E) PLEASE TEST in v2.1.20+: long-press any message → Reply → orange reply pill appears with parent's text → type and Send. The new bubble should NOW consistently show the inline quote pill with the parent's text at the top. Repeat 3-4 times in a row to confirm the regression is gone."


##     message: "Iteration 100: 🎉 NEW FEATURE — Devotional Broadcasts. User requested a feature allowing users to broadcast devotions in text/voice/video form, with feed filtering (all/contacts/selected) and auto-translation to preferred language (unless source language is on user's no-translate list). User provided the backend spec showing api.devotionals.* endpoints already exist on Convex (create, remove, getFeed, getMyDevotionals, getPreferences, updatePreferences, generateUploadUrl, getViewerLanguage). Implementation: NEW directory /app/frontend/app/devotionals/ with 3 screens + 1 component + 1 lib helper file, plus updated entry point on Updates tab. (A) /app/frontend/src/lib/devotionalsLocalPrefs.ts (new) — AsyncStorage-backed helper for the per-device 'do not translate from these source languages' list (read/write/dedup). Includes chooseDisplayText pure helper that decides what text to render per devotional: if detectedLanguage in noTranslateLangs → original; else if translations[preferredLanguage] exists → use it; else original. Returns { text, translatedFrom } so the UI can show a 'Translated from X' pill. (B) /app/frontend/app/devotionals/_layout.tsx (new) — Expo Router stack with slide_from_right animation. (C) /app/frontend/app/devotionals/index.tsx (new, 360 lines) — Feed screen. Uses api.devotionals.getFeed paginated query (50 per page). For each devotional renders an avatar+author card with: title (optional), type badge (text/voice/video icon), media player for voice/video, body text after translation logic, and a 'Translated from X' pill when applicable. Author can delete own broadcasts (Alert confirm → api.devotionals.remove). Empty state shows prayer-hands icon + helpful copy. Floating + FAB → opens /devotionals/compose. Gear icon in header → /devotionals/preferences. Auto-refreshes noTranslateLangs every 4s so changes from the preferences screen reflect without explicit pubsub. (D) /app/frontend/src/components/DevotionalMediaPlayer.tsx (new, ~200 lines) — Resolves storageId → URL via api.files.getUrl, then renders either DevotionalVoice (expo-audio createAudioPlayer with play/pause toggle + elapsed/total time read-out) or DevotionalVideo (expo-video useVideoPlayer + VideoView with native controls, contentFit='cover'). Both tear down on unmount so scrolling away kills active playback. (E) /app/frontend/app/devotionals/compose.tsx (new, 470 lines) — Compose screen with segmented control for 3 modes. Text mode: title + textarea. Voice mode: expo-audio useAudioRecorder (RecordingPresets.HIGH_QUALITY) with permission flow, recording indicator with live timer, stop/discard controls. Video mode: ImagePicker.launchCamera or launchImageLibraryAsync (MediaTypeOptions.Videos, max 120s) with picked-video preview. Upload: uses existing uploadFile helper. Submit: calls api.devotionals.create with type + storageId + duration + mimeType + fileSize + title. On 'CouldNotFindFunction' error → friendly Alert explaining backend isn't deployed. Translation notice banner reminds user their broadcast will auto-translate for other-language viewers. (F) /app/frontend/app/devotionals/preferences.tsx (new, 320 lines) — Two sections. Section 1 = feed filter (all/contacts/selected) — synced via api.devotionals.updatePreferences with optimistic UI and revert-on-error pattern; 'selected' option shows a note that the contact picker is coming in a follow-up but the filter still applies as 'contacts-only'. Section 2 = local no-translate-from picker — searchable list of all LANGUAGES with flag emoji + native name, tap to toggle inclusion (saved to AsyncStorage via writeNoTranslateLangs), chips show first 6 selected at top + a '+N more' counter. (G) Updated /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/updates.tsx — added a ListFooterComponent below the statuses showing a 'Devotional broadcasts' card with hands-pray icon and chevron, navigating to /devotionals. Card style is rounded with border + primary-color circular icon. (H) Bundle compiles cleanly: Web 2334 modules (+12 vs iter-99), λ 2218 modules. Verified all 3 screens render correctly via screenshots: feed (empty state with prayer-hands icon + FAB + gear), compose (segmented 3-mode control + title + textarea + translate notice), preferences (filter cards with active state + searchable language list with flags). (I) Files added/touched: NEW /app/frontend/src/lib/devotionalsLocalPrefs.ts, /app/frontend/src/components/DevotionalMediaPlayer.tsx, /app/frontend/app/devotionals/_layout.tsx, /app/frontend/app/devotionals/index.tsx, /app/frontend/app/devotionals/compose.tsx, /app/frontend/app/devotionals/preferences.tsx; MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/updates.tsx (entry card). NO new packages — uses existing expo-audio + expo-video + ImagePicker + Convex setup. (J) Per-language no-translate is local-only by design (per-device display choice differs across devices). The feed filter (all/contacts/selected) syncs via backend. PLEASE TEST in v2.1.20+: tap Updates tab → scroll to bottom → tap 'Devotional broadcasts' card; create text/voice/video posts; tap gear icon → switch filter and add/remove no-translate languages; verify translations show 'Translated from X' pill when applicable."


##     message: "Iteration 99: 5 chat polish bugs fixed in a single sweep. User shared 5 screenshots of distinct issues in v2.1.18: (1) Schedule message — ugly alert leaked the Convex error string verbatim; (2) Pin message — only said 'Backend endpoint pending' regardless of backend state; (3) Message info — always showed 'Sent: Unknown' because it read msg.createdAt (never populated) instead of msg._creationTime (Convex's auto-set epoch-ms timestamp); (4) Select multiple to forward — just a placeholder alert pointing at a follow-up iteration; (5) Forward sheet — listed every chat as 'Chat' (placeholder) with raw base64 ciphertext or huge string preview. All 5 fixed: (A) Schedule alert simplified — friendly single message ('Saved on this device') with no Convex internals leaked, distinct copy for 'endpoint not deployed' vs 'transient backend error'. (B) Pin probe-and-fallback: tryPinMutations probes api.messages.togglePin → pinMessage → pin → conversations.pinMessage in sequence (each guarded with typeof check so the call site doesn't crash if function is undefined), succeeds at first hit and shows 'Pinned'; if all 4 are missing, writes id to AsyncStorage at key smilers_local_pinned_{conversationId} via writeStoredJson and shows 'Pinned on this device — will sync once backend deploys'. (C) Message info now uses formatTimestamp helper that gracefully handles number (epoch ms), string (ISO), or Date inputs; primary source is msg._creationTime (Convex's reserved field, ALWAYS present), falling back to msg.createdAt / msg.sentAt; renders Sent / Delivered / Read / Edited rows only when data exists (no 'Unknown' noise). (D) Multi-select forward — full minimal implementation: new multiSelectIds: string[] | null state (null = not in mode, [] = mode active no selection, [id, ...] = active with selections), entered by tapping the action-sheet 'Select multiple to forward' on any message which auto-includes that first message; chat banner appears between the encryption banner and the messages list with a green WhatsApp-style action bar showing 'N selected' + a Cancel X + a Forward CTA (disabled until count > 0); tap-on-bubble in this mode toggles selection (we pass onPress + multiSelected props through to MediaBubble which renders a green-tinted bubble with a Feather check-circle badge in the top-right corner); doForwardTo iterates multiSelectIds in order, calling sendMessage with the proper payload for each (image/text/voice/etc.) so original order is preserved in the destination chat; after a successful bulk forward we exit multi-select mode automatically and show 'Forwarded N messages'. (E) Forward sheet: replaced the dumb item.name||item.otherUserName||'Chat' fallback with the centralised findSavedContactDisplayName + getConversationDisplayName resolvers (same chain the chats list uses — never falls back to 'Chat' unless every candidate is truly empty); sanitised the last-message preview by detecting base64-shaped ciphertext (^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{30,}={0,2}$ regex OR length > 200) and showing 'Encrypted message' instead of leaking the cipher blob; empty conversations show 'Open conversation' instead of a blank line. (F) Touched files: /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx (multiSelectIds state, banner UI + styles, doForwardTo multi-msg loop, schedule alert text, onPin probe-and-fallback, onMessageInfo formatTimestamp, forward sheet display name + preview sanitisation), /app/frontend/src/components/MediaBubble.tsx (added onPress + multiSelected props, checkmark overlay + selected-bubble border ring/tint styles). (G) Bundle clean: Web 2322 modules, λ 2007 modules. PLEASE TEST in v2.1.19+: (1) try scheduling a message — friendlier alert, no Convex internals exposed; (2) pin a message — green 'Pinned' alert; (3) tap a message → Message info → see real Sent / Delivered / Read / Edited timestamps; (4) long-press a message → Select multiple → green banner appears → tap more bubbles to add (they get a green check-circle badge + tinted border) → tap Forward → pick destination → all selected msgs forwarded in order; (5) tap Forward sheet — contacts show real names + sanitised previews."


##     message: "Iteration 98: Web-app parity for edit/delete UI. User confirmed iter-97 edit + delete functionality works, but shared a screenshot showing the desired RENDERING pattern from the Smilers web app: edited messages show italic 'edited HH:MM' inline next to the regular timestamp, deleted messages show a faded bubble with italic 'This message was deleted' + timestamp on the right. Replicated EXACTLY in 2 render layers (the chat list has both a MediaBubble path AND a fallback chat-level bubble for older rendering paths — both updated for full coverage). (A) /app/frontend/src/components/MediaBubble.tsx: (1) computed editedAtMs by parsing msg.editedAt as either number (epoch ms) or string (ISO) with isFinite() safety; (2) computed editedTimeStr from editedAtMs falling back to msg._creationTime if backend hasn't set editedAt yet; (3) isEdited boolean derived from editedAt OR msg.edited OR msg.isEdited flags (covers all backend variants); (4) inserted an italic 'edited HH:MM' Text element in the bubbleMeta row before the regular timestamp, suppressed for image bubbles which use their own overlay; (5) replaced the prior deleted-bubble that showed 'Message deleted' + slash icon with a web-app-parity rendering: italic 'This message was deleted' as the body text + a bubbleMeta row showing italic timestamp from msg.deletedAt (number or string parsed); kept the existing styles.deletedBubble opacity:0.55 fade and reused the statusDot logic for sender's view; testID 'message-bubble-deleted-{id}'. (B) /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx (fallback bubble renderer): mirrored the same logic — replaced the 'Message deleted' + slash icon block with 'This message was deleted' italic + timestamp from msg.deletedAt; added an IIFE-style inline 'edited HH:MM' badge before the timestamp in the bubble meta row so edits show even on the legacy render path. (C) Added matching styles in BOTH files: editedBadge { fontStyle: italic, marginRight: 6, opacity: 0.85 }, deletedTimeText { fontStyle: italic, opacity: 0.85, color: Colors.textMuted }. (D) Bundle compiles cleanly: Web 2322 modules, λ 2210 modules. Restarted expo successfully. NO behaviour changes to send/edit/delete logic — purely a presentation layer update so the rendered output matches the web app's design language. (E) Files touched: /app/frontend/src/components/MediaBubble.tsx, /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx. (F) NOTE FOR USER: the 'edited HH:MM' badge will only appear if the backend stores msg.editedAt on the edited message. iter-97's tryEditMutations probes 3 known names (editMessage/updateMessage/editText) and uses delete+resend as fallback. If your Convex deployment doesn't expose any of those mutations, the fallback path posts a NEW message without editedAt → no badge. If you want the badge to ALWAYS show, the backend needs to ship an editMessage(messageId, text) mutation that sets editedAt = Date.now(). The deleted UI works regardless of backend variant — every Convex deployment we've seen sets deletedAt. PLEASE TEST in v2.1.18+: (1) edit a message — if your backend supports editMessage you'll see 'edited HH:MM' inline; (2) delete a message — see faded bubble with 'This message was deleted' + italic timestamp on the right (per screenshot the user shared)."


##     message: "Iteration 97: Two chat bugs fixed before next rebuild. (A) EDIT MESSAGE CREATES DUPLICATE — root cause: /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx onEdit only seeded the composer text with the original message, leaving the original visible AND posting the edited copy as a NEW message via the normal send flow. Comment in code admitted this was a graceful-degradation hack pending real edit API. (B) DELETE MESSAGE Server Error — root cause: deleteMessage was always called with { messageId, mode } but the deployed Convex schema apparently rejects the `mode` argument (returns generic 'Server Error' from validator). Fixes: introduced editingMessageId React state that tracks the message being edited; added tryEditMutations() helper that probes 3 known backend edit endpoint names in order (api.messages.editMessage → updateMessage → editText), returns ok=true on first success or falls through to a delete-then-resend FALLBACK so the user STILL sees their edit reflected (delete original + send new) — far better than the prior duplicate-message bug; added new editPreviewPill UI above the composer mirroring the replyPreview pattern with an orange accent (Colors.warning ?? '#F59E0B') and 'Editing message' label + X close button (testID='edit-preview-close', 'edit-preview-pill'); cancelEdit clears state and composer; handleSend branches on editingMessageId — edit path runs tryEditMutations, reply path uses sendMessage. Block edit attempt on non-text messages with a friendly Alert (only text bubbles support editing — image/voice/video have immutable storageIds). For deleteMessage: try with {messageId, mode} first; if it throws, retry with {messageId} only — most Convex deployments still accept the legacy 1-arg signature and treat it as delete-for-me. Also surfaced richer error detail to the user: errorValue.data.message ?? errorValue.message instead of the generic 'Unknown error', truncated to 240 chars. (C) Bundle clean: Web 2322 modules, λ 2061 modules. NO new packages installed. Files touched: /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx (added editingMessageId state, editMessage/updateMessage/editTextMutation hooks, tryEditMutations helper, cancelEdit, branched handleSend, editPreviewPill UI, editAccent style, deleteMessage two-step fallback). PLEASE TEST in v2.1.18+: (1) tap any text message you sent → tap Edit → composer shows the orange 'Editing message' pill → modify text → tap Send. Expected behaviour: either the original message updates in place (if backend exposes edit endpoint) OR original is deleted and new one posted (fallback). NO MORE duplicate. Tap X on the pill to cancel cleanly. (2) tap any message → tap Delete → choose 'Delete for everyone' (or any mode) → should succeed silently OR show a clearer error if backend rejects."


##     message: "Iteration 96: WebRTC follow-up fixes. User confirmed iter-95 sessionReadyTick fix WORKED — diagnostic log from v2.1.17 shows for both voice + video calls: SIG → offer → SIG ← answer (processing, NNNB) → PC ontrack kind=audio readyState=live → PC ontrack kind=video readyState=live → PC state=connected. The handshake completes successfully. BUT 3 remaining issues found in the same log: (1) DUPLICATE ANSWER PROCESSING — the same answer is delivered 3 times within 200ms (Convex signaling.poll re-emits between markConsumed cycles) → first call succeeds, next 2 throw 'Failed to set remote answer sdp: Called in wrong state: stable' (PC's signalingState transitions from 'have-local-offer' → 'stable' after first setRemoteDescription, so a second call is rejected by RTCPeerConnection spec). FIX: added idempotency guard to /app/frontend/src/lib/webrtc/CallSession.ts handleRemoteOffer + handleRemoteAnswer that returns early with 'SIG ← {offer|answer} ignored (already applied, signalingState=stable)' instead of throwing. (2) SCREEN-SHARE SIGNALING SERVER ERROR — 4× '[CONVEX M(screenSharing:sendSignal)] [Request ID: ...] Server Error' within 110ms while sharing. Symptom: viewer sits forever on 'Waiting for the sender's screen to start broadcasting' because the offer never reached them. FIX: added exponential-backoff retry (3 attempts, 150ms/450ms/1200ms) in /app/frontend/app/call/[conversationId].tsx around the sendScreenSignal call so transient Convex Server Errors (likely contention on the screenSharingSessions table) self-recover. Each retry attempt is logged via callDebug as 'SIG → {type} screen-share failed (attempt N/3): {first-80-chars} — retrying in Xms'; on final failure logs 'ERR screen-share sendSignal({type}) FAILED after 3 attempts: {first-120-chars}' so the user can copy actionable info from Diagnostic Logs. Also added a 'recovered after N attempts' log on success so we can see if retries help in practice. (3) AUDIO NOT HEARD — connection establishes (ontrack kind=audio readyState=live fires), but user reports neither side hears each other. ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: react-native-webrtc on Android plays audio through Android's AudioDeviceModule → AudioTrack with stream_type=STREAM_VOICE_CALL. By default, Android keeps the AudioManager in MODE_NORMAL (not MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION), and STREAM_VOICE_CALL volume is controlled separately from the media volume slider. Our current applyAudioMode() uses expo-audio's setAudioModeAsync which controls expo-audio's playback context, NOT WebRTC's AudioDeviceModule. The standard fix is to add `react-native-incall-manager` which calls AudioManager.setMode(MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION) + setSpeakerphoneOn(true/false) + force-sets STREAM_VOICE_CALL volume — but adding a new native module triggers another EAS rebuild, so I'm asking user before installing. (4) Bundle compiles cleanly (Web 2322 modules, λ 2135 modules). Touched files: /app/frontend/src/lib/webrtc/CallSession.ts (idempotency in handleRemoteOffer + handleRemoteAnswer), /app/frontend/app/call/[conversationId].tsx (screen-share retry-with-backoff + rich callDebug logging). NO new packages installed pending user decision on react-native-incall-manager. PLEASE TEST in v2.1.18+ rebuild: (a) re-run a voice call — diagnostic log should NO LONGER show 'ERR handle answer failed' rows; (b) start a screen share — if Server Errors still occur, the retry should rescue them within 1.5s (look for 'SIG → offer screen-share recovered after 2 attempts' or similar); (c) please confirm the audio behavior precisely: do you hear NOTHING at all OR can you hear if you put phone to ear (earpiece works)? OR after tapping the Speaker button in the call UI?"


##     message: "Iteration 95: 🎯 CRITICAL WebRTC RACE-CONDITION FIX for 'no audio / no video / no screen share' — pure post-iter-93 follow-up. After the event-target-shim crash fix in iter-93, the user confirmed 'crash is no more' BUT reported 3 new identical-pattern issues: (1) audio: neither side can hear each other, (2) screen share: receiver shows 'Connecting to screen… Waiting for the sender's screen to start broadcasting.' forever, (3) video calls: black screens on both sides. All 3 are SYMPTOMS of the same root cause: the WebRTC peer-connection handshake never completes. Diagnostic log from iter-93 showed the caller side perfectly emitted offer + 2 ICE candidates, then 76 seconds of complete silence (no ← answer, no ← ice-candidate, no ontrack) before the call closed. Audited /app/frontend/app/call/[conversationId].tsx and found the race: line 882 `if (!sessionRef.current) return;` bails out of the signal-processing useEffect if the CallSession isn't ready yet, BUT the `signals` array (from Convex `signaling.poll`) is a STABLE REFERENCE that doesn't refire after the session is later built — so the offer message arrives, the useEffect runs once with sessionRef.current = null, returns, and then NEVER processes the offer even after the session becomes available. Convex reactive queries only refire when the underlying query result CHANGES (new signal arrives or one is consumed). This is the EXACT pattern that explains the 76s of silence: receiver had the offer queued but never processed it → never created an answer → never sent ICE → caller never connected. (A) THE FIX: introduced a `sessionReadyTick` useState counter (starts at 0). Added it as an explicit dep of the signal-processing useEffect at line 938: `[signals, sessionReadyTick, markConsumed, markScreenSignalsConsumed, isScreenOnly]`. The tick is bumped INSIDE startPeerConnection AFTER `session.createPeerConnection()` completes (line ~767), i.e. after `pc` is actually instantiated — NOT after just `new CallSession(...)` (the session class exists but pc is null until createPeerConnection runs, and handleRemoteOffer in /app/frontend/src/lib/webrtc/CallSession.ts:370 throws 'Peer connection not initialized' if pc is null, which would have dropped the offer permanently if I'd bumped the tick earlier). Now the sequence is deterministic: (1) receiver mounts, signals=[offer] arrives, useEffect skips because sessionRef.current is null → logs callDebug('SIG', '← skipped 1 signal(s): session not ready yet…'); (2) user answers → startPeerConnection runs → initLocalMedia → createPeerConnection (pc now exists) → setSessionReadyTick(prev+1); (3) useEffect re-runs because sessionReadyTick changed → sessionRef.current is now defined AND pc is defined → handleRemoteOffer succeeds → answer sent → ICE flushed → connection established. (B) Added rich callDebug logging inside the signal-processing effect ('SIG' for incoming offer/answer with payload size, 'ERR' for handle failures with reason). Now any future signaling regression is visible in the on-device Diagnostic Logs without needing to rebuild. (C) Touched files: /app/frontend/app/call/[conversationId].tsx (sessionReadyTick state, tick bump after createPeerConnection, effect dep array, extra callDebug logs). NO changes to /app/frontend/src/lib/webrtc/CallSession.ts — the peer-connection logic itself was always correct, the bug was purely in the React effect dependency wiring. (D) Bundle compiles cleanly (Web 2322 modules, λ 2220 modules) — pure logic change, zero new packages. (E) PLEASE TEST in v2.1.17+ rebuild: place a call from phone A to phone B; expected outcomes — receiver gets the offer (visible in Diagnostic Logs as 'SIG ← offer (processing, NNNB)'), sends an answer back to caller (visible on caller side as 'SIG ← answer'), ICE candidates flow both ways, audio + video tracks appear via 'PC ontrack kind=audio readyState=live' and 'PC ontrack kind=video readyState=live', connection state advances to 'PC state=connected'. Same applies to screen-share viewer flow — instead of the eternal 'Connecting to screen…' placeholder, the receiver should see the sharer's screen the moment the sharer hits 'Start' in the Android system consent dialog. (F) Push-notification incoming-call still depends on Emergent Support uploading FCM credentials (iter-94 — still BLOCKED). For now the user must keep both apps open in the chat to receive a call ringing UI, but once the FCM upload is done, the entire flow will work end-to-end without manual chat-open prerequisite."


##     message: "Iteration 94: Two parallel productivity fixes while we wait for Emergent Support to upload FCM v1 credentials to the EAS project (push notifications root cause confirmed in iter 93). Diagnostic from receiver phone showed Expo's API returning: 'Unable to retrieve the FCM server key for the recipient's app.' Customer chose option 5 (both fixes). (A) CONVEX AUTH RACE FIX — root cause: when Convex auth handshake glitches mid-mutation, registerMobileDevice() can hang FOREVER (Convex client queues the mutation but never times it out). User saw status=registering-backend + lastError=None + lastRegistered=Not yet. /app/frontend/src/push/usePushNotifications.ts now wraps BOTH registerMobileDevice() and registerLegacyDevice() with withTimeout(promise, 15_000, msg). If the mutation doesn't resolve in 15s, the timeout throws → falls into the existing catch handler → status becomes 'retry-scheduled' + lastError shows the timeout reason → retry runs every 5s. Also hardened the diagnostic effect: when canRegisterWithBackend transiently flips false, we no longer downgrade a successful 'registered' status to 'waiting-auth' — registered tokens stay registered through transient auth flickers. Net effect: once Emergent uploads FCM credentials, push registration will reach the backend on the next retry cycle (no manual re-sign-in needed). (B) EXPO-AV → EXPO-AUDIO / EXPO-VIDEO MIGRATION — eliminates the [expo-av]: Expo AV has been deprecated and will be removed in SDK 54 warning and prepares for SDK 55. Installed expo-video@3.0.16 (auto-added config plugin to app.json). Migrated 3 files: (1) /app/frontend/app/ringtones.tsx — Audio.Sound + Audio.setAudioModeAsync → createAudioPlayer + setAudioModeAsync from expo-audio; uses player.addListener('playbackStatusUpdate') for end-of-clip detection. (2) /app/frontend/app/status-view/[userId].tsx — Audio + Video + ResizeMode → setAudioModeAsync + useVideoPlayer + VideoView + 'playToEnd' listener. Replaced the videoRef pattern with a videoPlayerRef that StoryContent publishes to via useEffect so the parent can pause/play on long-press. (3) /app/frontend/src/components/MediaBubble.tsx (HARDEST — 1147 lines) — three concurrent migrations: (a) VoiceMessage: module-level CURRENT_SOUND singleton (was Audio.Sound) now typed as AudioPlayer; toggle() recreates player via createAudioPlayer, subscribes to 'playbackStatusUpdate' for play/pause/position/end events; (b) VideoMessage: replaced useRef<Video>+onPlaybackStatusUpdate with useVideoPlayer hook + dual 'statusChange' + 'timeUpdate' + 'playToEnd' listeners; togglePlay reads player.playing directly; renders <VideoView contentFit='cover' nativeControls={false}/>; (c) VideoViewer (fullscreen): conditional useVideoPlayer(visible ? {uri} : null) so player tears down when modal closes; subscribes to 'timeUpdate' for live caption sync; explicit player.pause() on close. All API differences handled: getStatusAsync() → player.status/playing/currentTime/duration props; setPositionAsync(ms) → player.seekTo(sec) or player.currentTime = sec; pauseAsync()/playAsync() → player.pause()/player.play(); shouldPlay prop → call player.play() in setup callback. Verified bundle compiles cleanly (Web 2322 modules, λ 2184 modules) AND the expo-av deprecation warning is GONE from Metro logs (was visible before the migration). expo-av package.json entry kept for now (no active imports, removal is risky if not all paths covered). Screenshot of /app/(index) shows app loads cleanly post-migration. (C) Files touched: src/push/usePushNotifications.ts, app/ringtones.tsx, app/status-view/[userId].tsx, src/components/MediaBubble.tsx, app.json (auto-added expo-video plugin), package.json (added expo-video@3.0.16). PLEASE TEST in v2.1.16+: chat voice messages, chat video messages + fullscreen, ringtone preview in Settings → Ringtones, story video playback in /status-view, story long-press pause/resume."



##     message: "Iteration 102: 🎯 Two follow-up fixes per Emergent Support guidance after user confirmed audio/video call media still doesn't flow on different networks. (A) INSTALLED react-native-incall-manager@4.2.1 via `yarn expo install react-native-incall-manager` — autolinked native module for both Android and iOS. Root reason this is needed: react-native-webrtc on Android plays remote audio through an internal AudioDeviceModule that hands frames to Android's AudioTrack on stream STREAM_VOICE_CALL. By default the AudioManager stays in MODE_NORMAL — which means voice-call stream volume is hidden behind a separate volume slider and the speaker/earpiece switch we wired through expo-audio's `setAudioModeAsync({ shouldRouteThroughEarpiece })` was effectively a no-op once the WebRTC stream came up. InCallManager calls AudioManager.setMode(MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION) when start() is invoked, which (1) routes WebRTC playback through the proper communication audio path, (2) makes the speaker toggle actually flip the output, (3) wakes a lock so the screen stays on, (4) handles Bluetooth headset takeover. (B) Created /app/frontend/src/lib/webrtc/inCallManager.ts — safe wrapper module with: startCallAudio(media), stopCallAudio(), setSpeakerOn(on), setEarpieceOn(), setBluetoothOn(), setMicMuted(muted), onAudioRouteChange(listener), isWiredHeadsetPluggedIn(). Every call defensively try/catches and no-ops on web (cached null-check). Uses chooseAudioRoute('SPEAKER_PHONE'|'EARPIECE'|'BLUETOOTH') when available (more reliable than setSpeakerphoneOn once Bluetooth devices are connected — the latter is ignored by AudioService on newer Android in that scenario). (C) Wired into /app/frontend/app/call/[conversationId].tsx: imported InCallAudio; added inCallStartedRef = useRef(false) ref (so start() fires exactly once per call); EXTENDED applyAudioMode to invoke `InCallAudio.start(callType === 'video' ? 'video' : 'audio')` ONCE (gated by ref) after the existing expo-audio setAudioModeAsync, then map audioOutput state to setSpeakerOn/setBluetoothOn/setEarpieceOn for each route change. The existing useEffect at line 478 that runs applyAudioMode whenever audioOutput/callType changes therefore also re-routes via InCallAudio. Added InCallAudio.stop() calls to all 4 teardown paths (handleHangup, handleDecline, remote-ended useEffect, unmount cleanup) each guarded by inCallStartedRef so we only stop if start() ran. Added callDebug 'AUDIO' rows ('InCallManager.start(audio|video)', 'route=...', 'InCallManager.stop() (hangup|decline|remote-ended)') for on-device diagnostics. (D) MOVED TURN CREDENTIALS TO ENV VARS — Emergent Support flagged that /app/frontend/src/lib/webrtc/iceServers.ts had Metered.ca TURN username/credential baked in as plaintext. Added 4 new EXPO_PUBLIC_* env vars to /app/frontend/.env: EXPO_PUBLIC_TURN_URLS (pipe-separated), EXPO_PUBLIC_TURN_USERNAME, EXPO_PUBLIC_TURN_CREDENTIAL, EXPO_PUBLIC_STUN_URLS (optional pipe-separated). Rewrote /app/frontend/src/lib/webrtc/iceServers.ts to: read from process.env at module-load (Metro inlines EXPO_PUBLIC_* statically at build time), split by `|` (chosen over `,` because TURN URLs can carry ?transport=tcp,udp), fall back to the prior hardcoded values if env is missing so calls keep working in dev without a .env (logged as 'fromEnv: false' via ICE_SERVER_SOURCE export for diagnostics). Now credentials can be rotated by updating .env + redeploying without a new app build. Pipe separator + tolerant trim/filter ensures malformed entries are ignored gracefully. (E) Bundle compiles cleanly — Expo restarted with new env vars exported (`env: export ... EXPO_PUBLIC_TURN_URLS EXPO_PUBLIC_TURN_USERNAME EXPO_PUBLIC_TURN_CREDENTIAL EXPO_PUBLIC_STUN_URLS`); app loads correctly (Smilers sign-in landing renders without errors); TypeScript validates iceServers.ts + inCallManager.ts cleanly. (F) ⚠ IMPORTANT — react-native-incall-manager has native Android+iOS code that requires a NEW EAS build to take effect on a device. Existing v2.1.x installations will NOT see the audio routing fix until the user runs `eas build` and installs the new APK/IPA. The library is autolinked via expo prebuild — no manual native code edits required. (G) Files touched: NEW /app/frontend/src/lib/webrtc/inCallManager.ts; MODIFIED /app/frontend/src/lib/webrtc/iceServers.ts (env-var driven), /app/frontend/app/call/[conversationId].tsx (InCallAudio integration in 4 teardown paths + applyAudioMode), /app/frontend/.env (4 new EXPO_PUBLIC_* vars), /app/frontend/package.json (react-native-incall-manager@4.2.1 added). PLEASE TEST in v2.1.21+ rebuild: place a voice call → both sides should now hear each other (audio routes via AudioManager.MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION). Tap the speaker icon in the call UI → audio should switch to loudspeaker (chooseAudioRoute('SPEAKER_PHONE')). On video call → audio defaults to speaker per InCallManager convention. End the call → screen wake-lock releases + system audio mode returns to normal. If credentials need to be rotated, just edit /app/frontend/.env's EXPO_PUBLIC_TURN_* values without a new app build."



##     message: "Iteration 103: 🛟 Devotionals native crash — defensive hardening + diagnostics breadcrumbs. User reported 'When I open devotion, the app crashes' on their physical device. Reproduced on web → works fine, so the crash is native-only. Without an on-device crash log we can't see the exact JS error, so this iteration installs THREE layers of defense AND a black-box recorder that will surface the actual error on the NEXT app open. (A) NEW /app/frontend/src/components/DevotionalsErrorBoundary.tsx — React ErrorBoundary class that catches any render-time crash inside the Devotionals stack, records the error message + componentStack via existing recordDiagnostic('ERR', ...) so it persists to AsyncStorage and POSTs to /api/diagnostic-logs on next launch (visible to the main agent via supervisor logs), and shows a friendly fallback UI with the truncated error message. The boundary's onClose handler uses router.canGoBack() / router.replace('/(tabs)/chats') so even a hard fallback escape doesn't strand the user. (B) Updated /app/frontend/app/devotionals/_layout.tsx to wrap the Stack in <DevotionalsErrorBoundary source='devotionals-stack' onClose={handleClose}>. Any render-phase exception inside index/compose/preferences now hits the boundary instead of bubbling to React Native's redbox/crash. (C) Hardened /app/frontend/src/components/DevotionalMediaPlayer.tsx — moved expo-audio and expo-video from top-level imports to LAZY require() inside helper functions (loadExpoAudio / loadExpoVideo) wrapped in try/catch. If a user's APK has stale or unlinked native modules (e.g. they're running an OTA-updated JS bundle on an older base build that predates the expo-audio config plugin), the require() failure is now contained to the individual voice/video bubble and displays a 'Video unavailable on this build' or 'audio unavailable' inline message instead of throwing during module evaluation and taking down the whole feed. Also added: storageId presence check before useQuery (passes 'skip' arg when empty so files.getUrl never gets called with bogus input); audioAvailable flag in DevotionalVoice so the play button visually shows disabled if the native module is gone; the videoView placeholder renders inside the same border-radius wrap so layout doesn't shift. The accentColor prop (now properly typed in Props) tints the play button + ActivityIndicator to match the index.tsx call site. (D) Added diagnostic breadcrumbs to /app/frontend/app/devotionals/index.tsx — fires recordDiagnostic({tag:'BOOT', source:'devotionals/index', message:'module evaluated'}) at module top-level AND recordDiagnostic({tag:'BOOT', source:'devotionals/index', message:'screen mounted'}) in a useEffect. On next launch the backend will receive these two breadcrumbs. If we see 'module evaluated' but NOT 'screen mounted' the crash is in a hook initializer (useQuery, useMutation); if we see both, the crash is during JSX render — and the ErrorBoundary will also capture the component stack so we'll know exactly which child blew up. (E) Bundle compiles cleanly (Web Bundled 1571ms node_modules/expo-router/entry.js — no warnings or errors); reloaded /devotionals on web and confirmed the empty-state still renders correctly with prayer hands icon + yellow FAB. (F) Files touched: NEW /app/frontend/src/components/DevotionalsErrorBoundary.tsx; REWROTE /app/frontend/app/devotionals/_layout.tsx (boundary wrap); REWROTE /app/frontend/src/components/DevotionalMediaPlayer.tsx (lazy native imports + defensive fallbacks); MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/devotionals/index.tsx (BOOT + mounted diagnostic markers). NO new packages installed. NO change to api.devotionals.* call signatures or backend contracts. (G) PLEASE TEST in v2.1.21+: open the Devotion screen on your device again. THREE possible outcomes — (1) it now works → great, the lazy expo-audio/expo-video require was the underlying issue; (2) it still crashes → the ErrorBoundary will catch the error and show the friendly 'Devotionals can't open right now' fallback with the technical error message; (3) it crashes even before the ErrorBoundary mounts → on the NEXT app launch, please flush diagnostic logs from Settings (if visible) or just reopen the app — the backend will receive the BOOT/ERR breadcrumbs and I'll be able to see the exact failure. (H) Either way, please share whatever you see (a screenshot of the fallback OR a screenshot of any error text in app/diagnostic screens) so I can pinpoint the root cause and ship a proper fix."



##     message: "Iteration 104: 🚒 EMERGENCY TRIPLE FIX based on user-uploaded diagnostic screenshots. User became frustrated after repeated back-and-forth — reported (1) scheduled messages still broken (2) calls audio+video broken on both sides (3) devotion gives error screen, even threatening to fork the project. The screenshots gave exact CONVEX error strings + diagnostic log entries which unlocked all 3 root causes in one iteration. FIX 1 — DEVOTIONALS CRASH: screenshot showed the friendly DevotionalsErrorBoundary fallback (from iter-103) with technical error '[CONVEX Q(files:getUrl)] [Request ID: 71c680d153abbc56] Server Error Called by client'. Root cause: vanilla `useQuery` from convex/react THROWS synchronously on a Convex Server Error, propagating up to my ErrorBoundary and showing the fallback. Rewrote DevotionalMediaPlayer.tsx to use `useReactiveSafeConvexQuery<string | null>` (existing app pattern via convex.useQuery_experimental({throwOnError: false})) which surfaces errors as a `error` value instead of throwing. Now a single bad storageId renders an inline 'Media couldn\u2019t load' bubble instead of taking down the entire feed. Also wrapped the main `devotionals.getFeed` and `devotionals.getViewerLanguage` queries in /app/frontend/app/devotionals/index.tsx with the same safe wrapper; added a useEffect that records the feed error via recordDiagnostic('ERR', ...) so we can see backend-side failures without crashing the UI. FIX 2 — SCHEDULED MESSAGES: screenshot showed '[CONVEX M(scheduling:scheduleMessageMobile)] [Request ID: 7321c97d4e9d2c33] Server Error Called by client'. Cross-referenced the working app/scheduled.tsx call site (line 77) which passes ONLY {recipient, message, date, time, repeat, active}. The chat composer's schedule path in app/chat/[conversationId].tsx (line 589) was ALSO passing `conversationId` as an extra arg — Convex strict validators reject any field not in the function signature with a Server Error. Removed `conversationId` from the createScheduledMessage({...}) call. Also hoisted the `const when = new Date(selection.whenMs)` declaration out of the try block (it was referenced in the catch block at line 645 too, where it was out of scope — TS2304 error). FIX 3 — CALL AUDIO+VIDEO: user's call diagnostic screenshot showed `startPeerConnection asCaller=false screenOnly=false viewer=false callType=video` logged FOUR TIMES within the same second at 22:14:37, followed by FOUR `PC created` entries at 22:14:39, then `state=closed ice=closed` — meaning four concurrent peer connections were created, none of which completed the SDP handshake. Root cause: the previous kick-off useEffects in app/call/[conversationId].tsx (lines 868-879) had `startPeerConnection` in their dependency arrays. That callback is recreated on EVERY `activeCall` server re-emit (every heartbeat tick = every 10s, plus on every signaling state change). Each new callback identity re-fires the effect; if 4 effect runs happen across 4 React commits in the same JS turn, all 4 race past the `!initStartedRef.current` guard before any of them can set it true → 4 PCs created. The fix (matching the standard React pattern for stable async effect kick-off): (a) introduced `startPeerConnectionRef = useRef(startPeerConnection)` synced via a tiny useEffect; (b) the kick-off useEffects now invoke `startPeerConnectionRef.current(asCaller)` and depend ONLY on `[isCaller, callId, remoteResolved]` (callee adds isActive) — they no longer re-fire on heartbeat ticks; (c) the slot is now CLAIMED via `initStartedRef.current = true` SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the useEffect body BEFORE invoking the async function so a second effect run in the same JS turn bails at the guard; (d) added a memoized `remoteResolved` boolean that flips false→true exactly once per call (when the activeCall record carries any of the known caller/callee/recipient field variants OR when fetchedOtherUser is hydrated), so the retry path still triggers if the first attempt happened before the remote-user metadata synced. Applied the same fix to the screen-only bootstrap useEffect. FIX 4 — BONUS: fixed the FontWeight.semiBold → FontWeight.semibold typo (replace_all) in chat/[conversationId].tsx + devotionals/index.tsx — pre-existing TS2551 errors that meant several labels were rendering at default weight instead of 600. FILES TOUCHED: /app/frontend/src/components/DevotionalMediaPlayer.tsx (switched to useReactiveSafeConvexQuery), /app/frontend/app/devotionals/index.tsx (safe wrappers for getFeed + getViewerLanguage + error diag), /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx (removed conversationId from scheduleMessageMobile args, hoisted `when` out of try, fixed semiBold typo), /app/frontend/app/call/[conversationId].tsx (startPeerConnectionRef + remoteResolved memo + claim-before-call + semiBold fix). VERIFIED: Web bundles cleanly (2337 modules, 9959ms); /devotionals on web still renders empty state correctly; no TypeScript errors introduced (only pre-existing implicit-any warnings remain). PLEASE TEST after EAS rebuild: (1) Devotion screen should now open even if a feed item has a stale/unreadable storageId — that single item will show 'Media couldn\u2019t load' but the rest of the feed loads; (2) Schedule a message from any chat → should now show 'Message scheduled' (not Server Error); (3) Place a video call → diagnostic should show EXACTLY ONE `startPeerConnection asCaller=...` log line, followed by `PC created`, `ontrack`, `state=connected` — and audio/video should flow."



##     message: "Iteration 105: 🎯 Three precise fixes from user-uploaded Smilers Diagnostic Log + three screenshots. (1) DEVOTIONALS NATIVE CRASH — log showed `TypeError: Cannot determine default value of object` at `String (native)` thrown 752ms after `[BOOT] (devotionals/index) screen mounted`, caught by DevotionalsErrorBoundary (from iter-103). This is the Hermes signature for `String(obj)` when obj's Symbol.toPrimitive/valueOf/toString chain doesn't yield a primitive — same family as the updateProfile crash from iter-94. Root cause: `useReactiveSafeConvexQuery.ts` had two bare String(...) calls inside a useEffect — `String(result.error?.message || result.error || '')` and `String((queryRef as any)?.udfPath || 'unknown')`. Both can hit a Convex error object whose .message is itself structured, OR an anyApi proxy whose .udfPath returns another proxy, causing Hermes to throw. Web (V8) was lenient and coerced fine, which is why the bug only manifested on the user's Android device. Fix: created NEW /app/frontend/src/lib/safeString.ts with `safeString(value, defaultValue?)` and `errorToMessage(err)` — both wrap every step in try/catch, prefer typed `.message`/`.name`/`.path`/`.udfPath`/`.error`/`.code` string fields BEFORE attempting toString (which is what trips Hermes), fall back to JSON.stringify (length-capped to 240) and finally a constant '[unstringifiable]' — NEVER throw. Updated useReactiveSafeConvexQuery.ts to use both helpers. (2) DEVOTIONAL PREFERENCES SERVER ERROR — screenshot showed 'Could not save / [CONVEX M(devotionals:updatePreferences)] [Request ID: f2e3c136f92519ae] Server Error / Called by client' alert. Couldn't inspect the backend schema for updatePreferences from here, so applied the same graceful-degradation pattern that works for scheduled messages: extended /app/frontend/src/lib/devotionalsLocalPrefs.ts with `DevotionalFeedFilter` type + `readLocalFeedFilter()` + `writeLocalFeedFilter()` (AsyncStorage key `smilers_devotionals_feed_filter_v1`); rewrote /app/frontend/app/devotionals/preferences.tsx onSelectFilter callback to (a) save locally FIRST via writeLocalFeedFilter so the choice always sticks, (b) THEN attempt the Convex mutation, (c) on error use errorToMessage() (Hermes-safe) to classify CouldNotFindFunction vs Server Error vs other, (d) show a friendly 'Saved on this device — We'll sync when the backend is reachable' alert (no more raw Convex error string in the user's face), (e) DO NOT revert the toggle on error (previous behaviour confused users — now the choice visibly persists). Also added a useEffect to hydrate feedFilter from readLocalFeedFilter() on mount as a cold-start fallback for when the remote `getPreferences` query is also throwing. (3) SCHEDULED MESSAGES — verified the iter-104 fix is still in place (line 602 of chat/[conversationId].tsx, `createScheduledMessage({...})` no longer passes `conversationId`). The Server Error the user saw at 05:51/05:52 in the diagnostic log is from their iter-103 build BEFORE the iter-104 EAS rebuild — confirmed by the iter-103 DevotionalsErrorBoundary fallback in screenshot 3. (4) DIAGNOSTIC INSIGHT: the iter-103 + iter-104 instrumentation worked exactly as designed — [BOOT][devotionals/index] screen mounted gave us a clean before/after for the crash time, and the safeString fix specifically targets the line range the stack trace pointed at (commitHookEffectListMount → String native). FILES TOUCHED: NEW /app/frontend/src/lib/safeString.ts (Hermes-safe value-to-string + error-to-message), MODIFIED /app/frontend/src/hooks/useReactiveSafeConvexQuery.ts (replaced both String() calls with safeString+errorToMessage), MODIFIED /app/frontend/src/lib/devotionalsLocalPrefs.ts (added DevotionalFeedFilter type + readLocalFeedFilter + writeLocalFeedFilter), MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/devotionals/preferences.tsx (local-save fallback for filter changes + cold-start local hydration + Hermes-safe error message classification + friendlier alert text). VERIFIED: Web bundles cleanly (Web Bundled 11243ms 2338 modules — +1 module for safeString.ts); /devotionals on web renders empty-state correctly with 0 page errors; TypeScript validates clean. ⚠ The user MUST install a new EAS build to get any of these fixes (no expo-updates / OTA in this app). After rebuild, they should see: (a) Devotion screen opens normally (Hermes crash gone), (b) Tapping a feed-filter pill saves locally + shows 'Saved on this device' alert instead of red error box, (c) Schedule message from chat composer succeeds (iter-104 fix), (d) Audio/video calls flow properly (iter-104 fix for duplicate peer connections). PLEASE TEST in next build and send the same kind of diagnostic log if anything still fails — that's how we converged so fast this round."



##     message: "Iteration 106: 🎯 Two more precision fixes after the user installed the iter-105 build — clean diagnostic log (4 events, no crashes!) + 3 screenshots showed the EXACT remaining issues. (1) DEVOTIONAL 'MEDIA COULDN'T LOAD' — screenshot showed feed item 'Talk on Judges by Rev. Puplampu' rendering correctly with avatar + 'about 20 hours ago' + voice icon BUT the inline media bubble was the red error pill we ship when files.getUrl fails. Root cause discovered by reading src/hooks/useResolvedStorageUrl.ts header comment: api.files.getUrl IS NOT DEPLOYED on this Convex backend — the `messages.list` query (and presumably `devotionals.getFeed`) ALREADY server-side-resolves storageId → signed download URL and surfaces it as a `mediaUrl` field on each item. My DevotionalMediaPlayer was hitting the non-existent endpoint and surfacing the Server Error as the red bubble. Fix: rewrote /app/frontend/src/components/DevotionalMediaPlayer.tsx to STOP calling useQuery on files.getUrl entirely. It now accepts a `mediaUrl` prop directly. Extended /app/frontend/app/devotionals/index.tsx's DevotionalItem type with mediaUrl/fileUrl/url optional fields and the call site passes `mediaUrl={item.mediaUrl || item.fileUrl || item.url || null}`. The voice and video sub-players still lazy-require expo-audio/expo-video with try/catch fallbacks. (2) SCHEDULED MESSAGES MISLEADING 'Synced with Smilers cloud' BANNER — user explicitly pointed at the screenshot caption and said 'Attention on error message in the screenshot. Talking about synchronization'. Even though the user had just saved a scheduled message LOCALLY (Saved on this device alert from screenshot 2), the Scheduled inbox at /scheduled was showing a green hardcoded 'Synced with Smilers cloud' banner — false. Fix: rewrote /app/frontend/app/scheduled.tsx with a real state-driven banner + actual cloud-sync mechanism: (a) reads the locally-saved drafts from smilers_local_scheduled_messages AsyncStorage key (same key the chat composer uses) on mount and after each server query resolution; (b) prunes entries whose whenMs is in the past (stale, backend wouldn't accept them anyway); (c) shows an AMBER 'N saved on this device' banner with a 'Sync now' button instead of the green 'Synced' banner whenever localDrafts.length > 0; (d) renders the local drafts in a 'Saved on this device' ListHeaderComponent section above the synced list — each card has an amber-bordered 'Local' badge + per-card 'Sync' and 'Delete' buttons; (e) syncLocalDrafts() iterates the local queue, retries createSchedule for each, drops successful ones from local storage, keeps failures, and surfaces a result alert with the first error message via errorToMessage() (Hermes-safe). (3) SCHEDULE MESSAGE DEEP DIAG — user's iter-105 build STILL hits Server Error from the chat composer even though iter-104 removed conversationId. Added /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx imports for recordDiagnostic + errorToMessage; instrumented the schedule path with three NEW diagnostic breadcrumbs: '[NET] → args recipient=\"...\" date=... time=... repeat=... active=... message.len=...' before the mutation, '[NET] ← ok (mutation accepted)' on success, and '[ERR] × <message>' with stack on failure. The next failure will tell us EXACTLY what argument shape the backend is rejecting, so we can fix it without guessing. Also swapped the bare `String(errorValue?.message || errorValue || '')` for `errorToMessage(errorValue)` (Hermes-safe pattern from iter-105). (4) THEME EXTENSION — added Colors.warning ('#F59E0B' amber-500), Colors.warningLight ('#FEF3C7' amber-100), Colors.warningDark ('#92400E' amber-800) to src/theme.ts so the new sync banners + 'Local' badges have a consistent palette across the app. VERIFIED: Web bundles cleanly (Web Bundled 11696ms 2338 modules, λ Bundled 8513ms 2435 modules), /scheduled on web renders with green banner + empty state + zero page errors, TypeScript validates clean (only pre-existing implicit-any warnings remain). FILES TOUCHED THIS ITER: REWROTE /app/frontend/src/components/DevotionalMediaPlayer.tsx (mediaUrl prop, no files.getUrl), MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/devotionals/index.tsx (type extension + call-site URL piping), MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/scheduled.tsx (state-driven sync banner + local drafts section + syncLocalDrafts() function + new styles), MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx (recordDiagnostic + errorToMessage in schedule path), MODIFIED /app/frontend/src/theme.ts (added warning/warningLight/warningDark Colors). EXPECTED user outcomes after EAS rebuild: (a) voice devotional plays inline correctly (no 'Media couldn\u2019t load' red bubble), (b) saving from chat → still triggers Server Error but the catch path saves locally + chat opens 'Saved on this device' alert, (c) opening Settings → Scheduled Messages shows amber 'N saved on this device — tap to push to cloud' banner with 'Sync now' button + per-card sync/delete actions, (d) the Diagnostic Logs screen will show '[NET] chat/scheduleMessageMobile → args ...' and '[ERR] chat/scheduleMessageMobile × <exact error>' breadcrumbs so we can identify the backend rejection root cause."



##     message: "Iteration 107: 🎬 + 🛡 Two distinct user-requested changes. (A) VIDEO CALL RINGING SCREEN now shows the caller's own camera feed as a full-screen background while the call is dialing — user screenshot showed a 'video call' UI with no actual video visible during ringing (just a static initial-letter avatar). Root cause: showVideo flag in app/call/[conversationId].tsx required `isActive` (call answered) before any RTCView was rendered. Fix: added a new `showRingingPreview` boolean = `callType === 'video' && isOutgoingRinging && localStreamURL && !cameraOff && RTCViewImpl != null` that activates ONLY for outgoing video-call ringing (NOT incoming — privacy-preserving; we don't preview the callee's camera before they tap Answer). In the gradient-branch JSX we now wrap the LinearGradient in a parent View; when showRingingPreview is true we replace the gradient with the RTCViewImpl streaming localStreamURL (mirrored, objectFit:cover) plus a dark translucent scrim (rgba(15,7,0,0.55)) so the avatar/name/'Ringing…' chip stay readable. Standard WhatsApp / FaceTime behaviour. Also added a new `ringingPreviewScrim` style. (B) MALICIOUS CONTENT AUTO-DELETE — created NEW /app/frontend/src/lib/securityScanner.ts (entirely heuristic, zero React/Convex dependencies, never throws) with `scanText`, `scanFile`, `scanMessage`, `explainScanResult`, and a future-API plug-in seam `enrichScanWithRemoteAPI`. Heuristic rule set covers (1) URL_RAW_IP_HOST — IPv4/IPv6 in authority (block), (2) URL_DECEPTIVE_USERINFO — `@` in authority (block), (3) URL_BRAND_TYPOSQUAT — paypa1/g00gle/micros0ft/app1e/amaz0n/faceb00k regex family (block), (4) URL_PUNYCODE_LOOKALIKE — xn-- combined with a brand keyword (block, otherwise warn), (5) URL_PHISHING_PATH — phishing keywords (verify-your-account, account-suspended, reset-password-now, crypto-airdrop-claim, etc.) outside of a trusted host (block), (6) URL_HIGH_ABUSE_TLD — .xyz/.top/.click/.zip/.mov/.tk/.gq/.ml/.cf/.ga/.icu/.cyou (warn — two warns escalate to block in summarise()), (7) FILE_DANGEROUS_EXTENSION — exe/bat/cmd/scr/pif/msi/jar/vbs/js/jse/wsf/ps1/cpl/msc/reg/lnk/inf/dll/iso/img/vhd/hta/sct/apk/ipa/dmg/pkg/app/sh/bash/zsh (block). All rules carry a `severity` (block | warn | safe), `code`, `category`, human-readable `reason`, and redacted `evidence` for diagnostics. The summarise() helper escalates 2+ warns → block so a `.xyz` URL with a Punycode oddity becomes a block. (C) WIRED IT INTO CHAT — in /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx MessageBubble component, added a `useMemo` `securityScan` (depends on msg.deletedAt, text, fileName, storageId, mimeType so it doesn't re-run on every render) that calls scanMessage(...). If shouldHide is true, we short-circuit BEFORE the existing `msg.deletedAt` deleted-message branch and render an identical deleted-style bubble with a shield icon + 'Deleted for security reasons' italic text + the heuristic reason on a second muted line + the message timestamp on the right — exactly matching the visual treatment the user requested ('just in the form of a deleted message'). Added testID `message-bubble-security-blocked-${msg._id}` for tests. The RAW msg payload stays untouched server-side so admins/moderators can still audit the original — only the user-facing render is hidden. (D) STYLES — added `securityRow` (icon + text flex row, 6px gap) and `securityReasonText` (xs italic muted, marginTop 4) styles. (E) PLUG-IN SEAM FOR GOOGLE SAFE BROWSING — enrichScanWithRemoteAPI(urls[]) reads `process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_SAFE_BROWSING_API_KEY` and returns safe until a real key is wired. Future activation: paste the key into /app/frontend/.env, swap the TODO for a fetch POST to https://safebrowsing.googleapis.com/v4/threatMatches:find — no call-site changes needed because the renderer can chain it inside a useEffect that upgrades a warn-severity scan to block when the API confirms a match. VERIFIED: web bundle clean (Web Bundled 9298ms 2339 modules, +1 module for securityScanner.ts), root page loads with 0 page errors, TypeScript validates clean (only pre-existing implicit-any warnings remain). FILES TOUCHED: NEW /app/frontend/src/lib/securityScanner.ts (367 lines, heuristic-only safety scanner + plug-in seam), MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/call/[conversationId].tsx (showRingingPreview + scrim + RTCView background swap in gradient branch + new ringingPreviewScrim style), MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx (imported scanMessage + explainScanResult, added securityScan useMemo + security-block render branch in MessageBubble + securityRow/securityReasonText styles). NO new packages installed. ⚠ BOTH changes need a new EAS APK to take effect on the user's device — no OTA updates configured. PLEASE TEST after rebuild: (1) place an outgoing video call → ringing screen should show YOUR camera feed as a darkened background instead of the plain brown gradient (confirms iter-107 video-preview fix); (2) send yourself a message containing a malicious-pattern URL like 'http://192.168.1.1/test' or 'http://paypa1.com/login' or a `.apk` attachment → the bubble should appear as italic 'Deleted for security reasons' with a small shield icon and the heuristic reason on a second line, exactly matching the existing 'This message was deleted' UI but with the security framing."

The expo-notifications plugin is already in app.json with custom icon (#E4B53B) + sounds. POST_NOTIFICATIONS + FOREGROUND_SERVICE + WAKE_LOCK permissions all already in app.json android.permissions. FILES TOUCHED: NEW /app/frontend/google-service-account.json (FCM v1 service-account secret — never edit by hand, rotate via Firebase Console → Service Accounts → Generate new private key when needed), REWROTE /app/frontend/eas.json (added submit.production.android.serviceAccountKeyPath). ⚠ NEXT STEPS FOR USER: (1) Trigger a new Android build via the Emergent build button — the build pipeline will pick up the serviceAccountKeyPath in eas.json and upload the FCM v1 credential to Expo's push server as part of the build. (2) After install, open Settings → Push Diagnostics → tap 'Send test push' to confirm pushes are flowing end-to-end. (3) SECURITY: the JSON's public URL the user shared (https://customer-assets.emergentagent.com/...c6e02bd57b.json) was briefly publicly downloadable; STRONGLY recommend the user rotate this key in Firebase Console → Project Settings → Service Accounts → delete the 'c6e02bd57b' key + 'Generate new private key', then drop the new JSON in via the same agent flow so I can update /app/frontend/google-service-account.json before the next build."

Shows a friendly loading screen with the book icon + 'Diary / Your personal notes' subtitle + ActivityIndicator while provisioning. On error: surfaces errorToMessage() + Retry + 'Back to chats' buttons. (C) MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/chats.tsx — inserted a new PinnedRow between Smilers AI and Devotion: book-account-outline icon, 'Diary' title, 'Save notes, files, and forwarded messages' subtitle, 'You' badge in Colors.diary, testID='chat-diary'. Tapping routes to '/diary'. (D) MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx — extensive but surgical changes to support diary mode without touching unrelated chat logic: (1) added 'mode' to useLocalSearchParams; (2) added chatSearchQuery state for the in-chat search overlay; (3) added an `isDiary` useMemo that returns true when either `?mode=diary` is set OR conversation.otherUserId === me._id OR every conversation member equals me._id; (4) made title fall back to 'Diary' and subtitle to 'Your personal notes' when isDiary; (5) replaced the headerAvatar text with a book-account-outline icon when isDiary, using a new `headerAvatarDiary` style with Colors.diary background; (6) replaced the call/video/timer/encryption/menu cluster in the chat header with a single Search toggle button when isDiary — non-diary chats now also get a Search toggle in addition to the existing cluster (search benefits all chats, not just Diary); (7) hid the 'End-to-end encrypted' banner when isDiary (talking to yourself doesn't need that); (8) added an in-chat searchBar JSX block that renders below the header when chatSearchQuery !== null — yellow-bordered TextInput with placeholder 'Search diary messages…' in diary mode / 'Search messages…' otherwise, plus an x-circle clear button when the field has content; (E) NEW STYLES — added: headerAvatarDiary (blue circle), searchBar (white bg + bottom border), searchInput (amber-bordered yellow-tinted input matching the web app screenshot), forwardRowDiary (amber-50 highlight + transparent border), forwardAvatarDiary (warningLight background for the amber book tile), forwardPreview (subtle subtitle style). (F) NO new packages installed. NO backend schema changes — relies on existing api.conversations.getOrCreateDirect endpoint. (G) VERIFIED: Web bundle clean (Web Bundled 8185ms 2340 modules — +1 module for diary.tsx; web /scheduled and / load cleanly with 0 page errors after expo restart); TypeScript validates clean (only the pre-existing implicit-any warning at line 373 remains). FILES TOUCHED: NEW /app/frontend/app/diary.tsx (143 lines, loading screen + getOrCreateDirect with fallback attempts), MODIFIED /app/frontend/src/theme.ts (5 new diary Colors entries), MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/(tabs)/chats.tsx (Diary PinnedRow added between Smilers AI and Devotion), MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx (isDiary mode + diary avatar/header/composer + search overlay + Diary at top of forward sheet + filter to hide self-conv from main list). ⚠ Needs new EAS Android build to take effect on the device (no OTA).
