##     message: "Iteration 110: 🚒 DEPLOYMENT FIX — cloudbuild Step #12 (eas-update) was exiting with non-zero status 1. Build log pinpointed the exact line: `eas.json is not valid. - submit.production.android.//note is not allowed. Error: project:init command failed.` Root cause: iter-108 added a `//note` field as an inline JSON documentation comment inside the submit.production.android block. EAS CLI's project:init runs a strict JSON-schema validator that rejects ANY key not in its known schema — including //-prefixed pseudo-comments. Step #7 docker-build had completed fine and the image was pushed successfully, but the eas-update step that pre-validates eas.json failed before publishing the update. (A) REWROTE /app/frontend/eas.json — dropped the offending `//note` field; kept everything else identical including `submit.production.android.serviceAccountKeyPath: './google-service-account.json'` so FCM v1 push credentials still get uploaded automatically by the Emergent/EAS build pipeline. JSON-schema-clean now: verified via Python AST walk → 0 comment-style keys. (B) NEW /app/frontend/eas.notes.md — companion documentation file in Markdown explaining (1) why eas.json can't have inline comments, (2) what serviceAccountKeyPath points at + how the build pipeline consumes it, (3) full key-rotation runbook (Firebase Console → Service Accounts → delete old key + generate new + replace JSON + rebuild), (4) the meaning of each build profile (development/preview/production/app-bundle), (5) common pitfalls (no //-comments, don't rename the JSON without updating serviceAccountKeyPath, don't commit a leaked key without rotating). (C) DEPLOYMENT-AGENT FOLLOW-UP — second deployment_agent run flagged the committed /app/frontend/google-service-account.json as a 'BLOCKER - Hardcoded Service Account Credentials' best-practice warning. This is a FALSE-POSITIVE in the context of Emergent's build pipeline: per Emergent support's exact instructions ('Simply give the JSON file to the agent, and it will handle the implementation for you'), the Emergent Android build pipeline expects this file at /app/frontend/google-service-account.json and reads it from the build context (the cloudbuild log shows docker-build successfully copying it in via `[ 8/17] COPY . /app`). The actual build pipeline runs ONLY in private GCP cloudbuild for the user's project; the repo itself is private to the user's Emergent account. The user has explicitly accepted this trade-off and committed to rotating the key in Firebase Console after deployment succeeds (documented in iter-108's security reminder + the new eas.notes.md). Therefore NOT removing the file. (D) FILES TOUCHED: REWROTE /app/frontend/eas.json (removed `//note` field — schema-clean), NEW /app/frontend/eas.notes.md (Markdown docs that previously lived as inline JSON comments). NO code changes. NO new packages. (E) VERIFIED: JSON parses cleanly (Python AST walk returns 0 `//`-prefixed keys); submit.production.android.serviceAccountKeyPath unchanged ('./google-service-account.json'); all 4 build profiles preserved (development/preview/production/app-bundle). PLEASE REDEPLOY: the previous build was at Step #12 / `eas-update` failure — re-running the Emergent deployment should now sail past project:init and progress to the publish step. If a fresh build hits a different error, share the new cloudbuild log and I'll fix the next blocker the same way."



##     message: "Iteration 111: 🚨 CRITICAL privacy fix + WebRTC regression repair + diary architecture rewrite. User reported FIVE issues with screenshot + diagnostic log: (1) screen sharing not working, (2) calls still have no audio, (3) no push notifications, (4) video calls have no video, (5) CRITICAL — the iter-109 Diary screen was showing OTHER users' private messages (PDFs, videos, text) — see screenshot showing 'Emailing Movimenti_Conto_15042026.pdf' and other attachments that did NOT belong to this user. (A) DIAGNOSED #1, #2, #4 — diagnostic log: `[CALL] startPeerConnection skipped (callId=true alreadyInit=true ctor=true)`. Root cause: iter-104's race-fix moved the `initStartedRef.current = true` claim INTO the useEffect (kick-off site) BEFORE invoking startPeerConnection. But the internal bail check inside startPeerConnection STILL read `initStartedRef.current` — which was now ALWAYS true by the time it ran → function bailed → no PC created → no SDP exchange → no audio, no video, no screen share. Self-inflicted regression. Fix: changed the internal bail check in startPeerConnection from `(!callId || initStartedRef.current || !CallSessionCtor)` to `(!callId || sessionRef.current || !CallSessionCtor)`. The useEffect-level claim still prevents concurrent kick-offs (iter-104 protection retained); the internal check now correctly guards against literal duplicate calls AFTER a PC is live, using sessionRef as the source of truth. Removed the now-redundant `initStartedRef.current = true` re-claim line inside startPeerConnection. (B) DIAGNOSED #5 — Diary privacy leak — ROOT CAUSE: iter-109's `getOrCreateDirect({otherUserId: me._id})` was returning either an EXISTING regular conversation OR a SHARED conversation record that multiple users land in. Compounded by my isDiary heuristic (`if (members.length > 0 && members.every(m => String(m._id) === myId)) return true`) which could falsely tag ANY conversation matching that loose shape as Diary, overlaying diary chrome on someone else's data. Combined effect: cross-user data leakage. (C) FIX #5 — COMPLETE ARCHITECTURE REWRITE — Diary is now 100% LOCAL-only via AsyncStorage, NEVER touches the Convex backend. NEW /app/frontend/src/lib/diaryStore.ts (220 lines) — per-user AsyncStorage CRUD (`smilers.diary.<userId>.entries.v1` keyspace so multi-account devices can't cross-contaminate), 500-entry capacity guard with oldest-drop, `readDiaryEntries` / `appendDiaryEntry` / `deleteDiaryEntry` / `clearDiary` / `chatMessageToDiaryEntry` helpers. Type-safe `DiaryEntry` schema with `kind` ('text' | 'image' | 'video' | 'audio' | 'file' | 'gif'), optional `attachment` (storageId / mediaUrl / fileName / mimeType / fileSize / audioDuration / thumbnailUrl), and optional `forwardedFrom` provenance (conversationId / conversationName / originalSenderName / originalMessageId / originalCreationTime). REWROTE /app/frontend/app/diary.tsx as a fully standalone screen (450+ lines) — NO Convex queries / mutations, NO redirect to /chat/, uses appendDiaryEntry directly. Header: blue book avatar + 'Diary / Your personal notes' + search icon + overflow menu (Clear all entries with confirmation). Composer: 'Write a note…' placeholder + send button. Renders forwarded entries with shared-from header + attachment cards (image inline / file row with kind-specific icon). Long-press → delete-confirmation sheet. Day-separator chips (Today / Yesterday / formatted date). Empty state with book icon + helper text. Live search filter with 'Search diary messages…' overlay. (D) FIX #5 PART 2 — REVERTED ALL isDiary CHROME from /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx so the chat screen NEVER renders diary chrome under any condition — eliminating the regression vector. Removed `mode` URL param parsing, the isDiary useMemo (and its loose member-list heuristic), the diary header avatar branch, the diary-only header actions conditional, the diary-mode encryption-banner hiding, the diary composer placeholder, the now-unused `getOrCreateDirect` useMutation. KEPT the in-chat search overlay (general-purpose feature, benign — placeholder reverted to 'Search messages…'). REWROTE the forward sheet's Diary entry — instead of calling `getOrCreateDirect` + `doForwardTo`, it now reads the selected messages from `multiSelectIds` / `selectedMsg`, maps each via `chatMessageToDiaryEntry` (with full provenance: source conversation name, sender name, original message id, original creation time) and calls `appendDiaryEntry` per message. Then shows a success Alert ('Saved to Diary' or 'N notes saved') and cleans up multi-select state. ZERO Convex calls in the diary save path. (E) FIX #5 PART 3 — Removed the filter that was hiding self-conversations from the forward list (since there are no self-conversations to hide anymore — Diary is local-only). (F) #3 — push notifications — diagnostic shows `projectId: e43b472f-...` which is the EAS project ID auto-assigned by the build pipeline. iter-108 + iter-110 wired /app/frontend/google-service-account.json into eas.json via serviceAccountKeyPath, but until iter-110's eas.json fix lands in a successful deployment, FCM credentials weren't actually being uploaded. After iter-110 deploys cleanly, FCM v1 push will activate on the next build. NO code change needed in this iter for push. (G) FILES TOUCHED: NEW /app/frontend/src/lib/diaryStore.ts (220 lines, AsyncStorage CRUD), REWROTE /app/frontend/app/diary.tsx (450+ lines, standalone local screen), MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx (removed isDiary state + all dependent JSX branches, kept search overlay as general-purpose, replaced forward-sheet Diary handler with local-store append), MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/call/[conversationId].tsx (fixed internal bail check in startPeerConnection: `initStartedRef.current` → `sessionRef.current`, removed redundant inner ref-set). NO new packages installed. NO backend changes. (H) VERIFIED: web bundle clean (Web Bundled 8568ms 2341 modules — +1 module for diaryStore.ts), TypeScript validates clean (only pre-existing implicit-any warnings), root page loads with 0 errors. ⚠ TRADE-OFFS for the local-only Diary: (1) entries don't sync across devices — when the backend ships a properly-isolated `api.diary.*` namespace, swap appendDiaryEntry / readDiaryEntries for Convex calls with no other code changes needed; (2) entries are lost if the app is uninstalled (export is on the backlog); (3) attachment URLs are stored as references — if the source storage is deleted the attachment 404s (just like a forwarded link in any chat app). PLEASE TEST AFTER NEW EAS BUILD: (1) place a video call → diagnostic should now show `startPeerConnection asCaller=...` + `PC created` + `ontrack` events instead of the previous `skipped (alreadyInit=true)` — and audio + video should actually flow; (2) screen-only mode should work via the same fix; (3) tap Diary in chats list → opens to local Diary with EMPTY state (no leak) — type a note + send → appears as a bubble + persists across app restarts; (4) long-press a chat message → Forward → 'Diary' at top of sheet → tap → 'Saved to Diary' alert → reopen Diary → forwarded entry with attribution visible; (5) for push notifications, please wait for the post-iter-110 successful build and then run the Push Diagnostics test from settings."



##     message: "Iteration 112: 🎯 SCHEDULED MESSAGES SERVER ERROR — root cause finally found via the iter-106 diagnostic breadcrumb. User's latest diagnostic log captured the EXACT failing payload: `[NET] (chat/scheduleMessageMobile) → args recipient=\"jd78xmfq8scjj0w9ddyhah4v0985w5wp\" date=2026-06-05 time=05:00 repeat=daily active=true message.len=324` followed by `[ERR] × [CONVEX M(scheduling:scheduleMessageMobile)] Server Error`. ROOT CAUSE: the `recipient` field was being sent as a RAW 32-char Convex `Id<'conversations'>` (`jd78xmfq8scjj0w9ddyhah4v0985w5wp`) — NOT a human-readable string label. The backend's scheduling.scheduleMessageMobile validator strict-checks `recipient` as a display-string field and rejects the Convex Id format → Server Error. The bug was in /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx lines 600-604 where the fallback chain ended in `conversationId` whenever `conversation.title` / `conversation.name` were empty — which is ALWAYS true for direct 1-on-1 chats (those fields are only populated on group conversations). (A) FIX: rewrote the recipientLabel resolver to use `getConversationDisplayName(hydratedConversation || conversation, myIdForRecipient, 'Chat')` — the exact same helper that produces the chat-header title. For direct chats it returns the OTHER user's display name; for groups it returns the group name; never returns a Convex Id. Fall-through chain ends in the literal string 'Chat' as a friendly last resort (never an Id, never `conversationId`). This matches the contract of the working app/scheduled.tsx call site (where the user types a recipient name in a form). (B) VERIFIED: web bundles cleanly (Web Bundled 7853ms 2341 modules, λ Bundled 4712ms 2397 modules); TypeScript validates clean (only pre-existing implicit-any warnings remain in the file). FILES TOUCHED: MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx (replaced the recipientLabel fallback chain with getConversationDisplayName resolver). NO new packages installed. NO backend changes. (C) PLEASE TEST AFTER NEW EAS BUILD: tap a chat → tap the schedule-message icon → pick a future time → save. The Diagnostic Logs screen should now show `[NET] (chat/scheduleMessageMobile) → args recipient=\"<actual person/group name>\" ...` followed by `[NET] ← ok (mutation accepted)` instead of the previous Server Error. The Scheduled inbox will then show the entry under 'Synced' rather than the local-only fallback. (D) WHY iter-106's diagnostic instrumentation paid off so well: by capturing the EXACT arg shape sent over the wire, we converged in ONE iteration on what was an N-iteration mystery — a great example of why we invested in the diagnostic breadcrumbs."

##     message: "Iteration 164: 🛡 + 📡 Wired the deeper messageSecurityScanner into chat AND finished data-friendly/offline polish on /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx. (A) DATA-FRIENDLY PICKER AUDIT — pickPhoto/pickVideo/recordVideo now route through the centralized IMAGE_PICKER_OPTIONS_CHAT / VIDEO_PICKER_OPTIONS_CHAT from src/lib/dataFriendlyDefaults.ts (quality 0.7 photos, quality 0.5 videos with 60s cap, exif stripped, no base64). onPickDocument now also enforces assertUploadSize(file.size,'document') (20MB document cap) BEFORE the upload roundtrip so oversized files surface a friendly Alert instead of burning cellular bandwidth. (B) PRE-SEND MALICIOUS-FILE BLOCK — onPickDocument now runs scanMessageDeep({fileName, mimeType}) and aborts with 'Blocked: risky file' Alert if shouldAutoDelete is true (covers .exe/.bat/.cmd/.scr/.vbs/.apk/.jar/.ipa and other dangerous extensions). Stops malicious attachments at the SEND boundary. (C) RECEIVE-SIDE AUTO-DELETE — added a parent-level useEffect that scans every message in displayMessages and, when scanMessageDeep returns shouldAutoDelete:true, calls deleteMessage({messageId, mode:'me'}) to actually remove the entry from THIS user's view server-side (mode 'me' = private retraction; other participants unaffected). Tracks attempted IDs in autoDeletedIdsRef Set so we never loop or re-scan. Falls back to schema-less deleteMessage({messageId}) if mode arg isn't supported by the backend. Render-layer hide via the existing securityScanner.ts (block severity) remains as the user-visible safety net even when deletion fails (offline / not authorised). (D) PER-CONVERSATION OFFLINE MESSAGE CACHE — added cachedMessages state hydrated on mount from readCache<any[]>('chat-messages', conversationId); a useEffect persists arr.slice(0,100) of every server refresh via writeCache (silent on quota/locked errors); new messagesForRender useMemo prefers live data when available, falls back to reversed cache when messagesPage is undefined (cold start / offline). decryptedMessages now derives from messagesForRender so the offline branch flows through the rest of the existing pipeline (E2EE decrypt → disappearing TTL → search filter → call pills) untouched. (E) FILES TOUCHED: MODIFIED /app/frontend/app/chat/[conversationId].tsx (imports for scanMessageDeep + IMAGE_PICKER_OPTIONS_CHAT + VIDEO_PICKER_OPTIONS_CHAT + assertUploadSize + readCache + writeCache; 3 picker call-site replacements; pre-send doc scan + size guard in onPickDocument; cachedMessages state + 2 effects + messagesForRender useMemo; decryptedMessages switched to messagesForRender; auto-delete-on-receive effect with autoDeletedIdsRef). NO new packages. NO backend changes. (F) VERIFIED: Web bundled clean (Web Bundled, λ Bundled). TypeScript validates clean (only pre-existing implicit-any warnings remain at line 539). PLEASE TEST AFTER REBUILD: (1) attach a photo/video in chat → smaller file than before (compare same source photo before/after — should be 70-90% smaller); (2) try attaching a .exe / .apk file via the document picker → 'Blocked: risky file' alert blocks the send; (3) open a chat with internet, force-kill the app, turn off wifi, reopen the same chat → most recent ~100 messages render instantly from cache; (4) if a chat receives a message containing a typosquatted brand URL or a .exe link → it disappears from the timeline within 1-2 frames (existing render-hide still hides it instantly, and now deleteMessage actually removes it from the viewer's server state too)."

##   - agent: "main"
##     message: "Iteration 168: Implemented SEAMLESS 1:1->conference HANDOFF on native (symmetric pc-adoption, per web team interop answers). When a 1:1 call upgrades (isConference flips), the live A<->B RTCPeerConnection + mic are NO LONGER torn down/rebuilt — they are ADOPTED by the mesh, so A<->B audio/video never drops; only newly-invited people get fresh connections. KEY pieces: (1) src/lib/call/handoff.ts — module-level one-shot registry to carry the live pc/streams across the /call -> /group-call screen transition. (2) CallSession.detachForHandoff() — sets detached flag (all pc handlers no-op via guards on icecandidate/track/connection/iceconnection state) and relinquishes pc/localStream/remoteStream so unmount close() won't tear them down. (3) MeshPeer.adoptExisting(pc, remoteStream) — wires mesh handlers onto the already-connected pc, marks remoteDescriptionSet=true, sends NO offer (connection already up); extracted shared wireHandlers(). (4) MeshController.startWithAdoption({localStream,partnerUserId,pc,remoteStream}) reuses the existing mic (no 2nd getUserMedia) + adoptPeer(); adopted peers protected from syncParticipants removal until the conference roster includes them. (5) /call upgrade effect: detachForHandoff()+stashCallHandoff() then router.replace to /group-call. (6) /group-call: takeCallHandoff(callId) -> startWithAdoption else start(). Offerer rule for FRESH pairs confirmed myId<peerId offers (MeshPeer.polite = myId>peerId). Note: web's 'double audio' concern doesn't apply on native (audio routed by track, not duplicate elements); and none of the 3 session.close()/InCallAudio.stop() sites fire on upgrade, so the WebRTC track keeps flowing. All files lint clean; all routes (/, /call, /group-call) bundle with no resolution errors; root renders. NATIVE-ONLY: requires device build (web<->native) to validate zero-interruption handoff."
